messages.subject: Defining a sample
parts:
Dear all,

I am analysing some distance-sampling cetacean data which was
collected opportunistically. I have post-stratified my survey area
into regular blocks (ICES grid squares so that relationships can be
investigated against fisheries catch data) and all effort and
sightings have been assigned to their appropriate blocks. My
questions:

1) what should my basic sampling unit be within each block? Some
transects of survey effort are now segmented and so should a sample
(leg) be an individual segment of effort or should legs of effort
completed during a single day within a block represent one sample?

I believe that the latter would be more appropriate if variance is to
be estimated using the bootstrap method.

2) because of the opportunistic way in which data were collected,
some legs of effort are fairly close together (2km) and run
approximately parallel to each other, but were surveyed a week or
more apart. Does this cause problems in the analysis of density?

Any advice welcome. Many thanks

Kelly
